falsification_gate.description: Cluster-conditional consolidate-vs-expand split shows >=60/40 in at least one cluster. Tests whether endgame strategy is regime-specific.
falsification_gate.verdict: Gate is OVERPASSED globally — endgame is NOT regime-specific because the overwhelming pattern is consistent expansion. The 60/40 split was meant to identify a regime-flip; instead we get 76%/2% one-way. Re-interpret: endgame expansion is UNIVERSAL, not regime-conditional.

headline_findings: OVERWHELMING signal: 45/59 (76%) top-10 winners INCREASED ship share by >2pp in the final 100 turns. Only 1/59 contracted by >2pp.
Median ship-share gain across the last 100 turns is +16.7 percentage points — winners are still pulling ahead at the bell.
45/59 (76%) of winners made at least one successful enemy-territory capture in the final 50 turns. Late offence is the norm, not the exception.
CONTRADICTS the 'consolidate late' intuition: do NOT switch to defensive reinforcement in the closing turns. Keep attacking enemy planets.

Strategic implication: any 'endgame mode switch' that throttles aggression after turn ~400 is leaving win-rate on the table. The v7 search horizon's value head should NOT depreciate the value of late expansion.
Note: 'expand' here is measured on a WINNING agent — survivor bias may exaggerate. The corrective: when LOSING in the late game, this corpus has no data and we cannot generalise.
downstream_uses: Feeds Experiment Option 4 (endgame mode switch) — but now points the opposite way: DON'T add a switch; if anything, ensure the agent does NOT throttle near the end.
Could also feed a 'when winning, keep attacking' multiplier in v7's value head.
